t:
Chapter 63, relating to retirement for age, is amended by inserting before section 1263 the following new section:


“§ 1251. Age 62: regular commissioned officers; exceptions

“(a) 
Unless retired or separated earlier, each regular commissioned officer of the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps (other than an officer who is a permanent professor, director of admissions, or registrar of the United States Military Academy or United States Air Force Academy or a commissioned warrant officer) shall be retired on the first day of the month following the month in which he becomes 62 years of age. An officer who is a permanent professor at the United States Military Academy or United States Air Force Academy, the director of admissions at the United States Military Academy, or the registrar of the United States Air Force Academy shall be retired on the first day of the month following the month in which he becomes 64 years of age.


“(b) 
Notwithstanding subsection (a), the President may defer the retirement of an officer serving in a position that carries a grade above major general or rear admired, but such a deferment may not extend beyond the first day of the month following the month in which the officer becomes 64 years of age. Not more than ten deferments of retirement under this subsection may be in effect at any one time.”.

fable.w: This section sets mandatory retirement ages for regular commissioned officers and lets the President defer retirement for certain senior officers. The only decision-makers and affected persons (the President and military officers) are inside the federal government, and there is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving outside parties. The discretionary deferral might look like a decision process, but it involves no external input.
fable.s: the President may defer the retirement of an officer serving in a position that carries a grade above major general or rear admired

qwen_block.w: This section establishes mandatory retirement ages for military officers and grants the President discretion to defer retirement for a limited number of high-ranking officers. It does not involve consultation with, or participation by, any parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities). The actors involved are federal officials (the President) and federal employees (military officers).
qwen_block.s: Unless retired or separated earlier, each regular commissioned officer of the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps... shall be retired on the first day of the month following the month in which he becomes 62 years of age.

opus.w: This section sets mandatory retirement ages for regular commissioned officers and lets the President defer some retirements. Every actor named (the President and military officers) is inside the federal government. Although the President makes a decision here, nobody outside the government takes part in it, so this is not participation. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
opus.s: Notwithstanding subsection (a), the President may defer the retirement of an officer serving in a position that carries a grade above major general or rear admired
opus.b: Someone might read the President's power to defer retirements as a decision process that involves others. It doesn't. The deferral is the President's call alone, and it concerns military officers, who are federal personnel. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and the section creates no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the mandatory retirement age for regular commissioned officers and grants the President the authority to defer retirement for certain high-ranking officers. All actors involved (the President, the officers) are inside the federal government. There is no requirement or recommendation to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties, such as state governments, the public, or private organizations. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Notwithstanding subsection (a), the President may defer the retirement of an officer serving in a position that carries a grade above major general or rear admired, but such a deferment may not extend beyond the first day of the month following the month in which the officer becomes 64 years of age.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the President's discretion to defer retirement involves some form of consultation or decision-making process that could imply participation. However, the text strictly defines the authority and limits of the President's action regarding federal employees (officers). There is no mention of consulting with outside parties, state governments, the public, or any non-federal entities. The decision is made entirely within the executive branch (the President) regarding federal personnel.
